docs.guardRails: Hub administration and its guard rails

status.live: Implemented end to end with automated tests. Not yet deployed to production anywhere.
status.demo: The screen exists and is tested, but it runs on synthetic data and nothing is saved.
status.contract: The data shapes and rules are frozen as contracts; no storage or screen yet.
status.designed: An accepted design describes it; no code yet.
status.proposed: Designed for the first time and open for review.

mode.fake: A built-in imitation for trying the hub: nothing reaches a real provider.
mode.manual: A person does the work outside the engine, for example a register look-up.
mode.live: A real provider, enabled by a second person after a synthetic test.

hub.definition: One gathering point for a country or a city, with its own staff, settings and launch gates.

node.definition: One installation of the engine; it can host several hubs.

lifecycle.definition: Draft, preparing, soft launch, public, suspended, closing or closed; moving forward needs passed gates and a second person.

elevation.definition: A console session opened after your password and second factor; it ends after inactivity.

secondPerson.definition: A sensitive change is asked by one staff member and approved by another; nobody approves their own request.

digest.definition: A fingerprint of the exact change; an approval binds it, so any later change voids the approval.

killSwitch.definition: Stops a capability at once; one person engages it, releasing needs a second person and an incident note.

launchGate.definition: A condition with evidence that must pass before soft launch or public; there is no waiver.

configVersion.definition: Settings are never edited in place: each change is a version that is activated and later superseded.

demoData.definition: Synthetic, labelled records; never indexed, never federated, purged before soft launch.

caseGrant.definition: The only way staff see private data: scoped to a case, at most 72 hours, approved by a second person, every read logged.

keys.skip: The first Tab reaches “Skip to content”.
keys.order: Then the band, the navigation, the page heading and the content, in that order.
keys.menu: On a phone the sections open from the “Sections” button as a full-height sheet; Escape closes it.
keys.forms: Every change needs a reason; the result is announced and shown as a notification.

identity.title: Identity and territory
identity.lede: Who and where the hub is: names in every hub language, territories, languages, currency and time zone.
identity.name: Name
identity.territoriesNote: Territories describe where the hub works; they are never exclusive, and restricted places are refused at every level.
identity.versionsNote: Saving creates a new configuration version; the active one stays until the new version is activated.

modes.title: System modes
modes.lede: How the hub behaves: lifecycle stage, data, registration, moderation, automation, indexing and maintenance.
modes.blockedBy: Soft launch is blocked by open gates: {items}.
modes.demoRule: Demo data never leaves the hub, is never indexed or federated, and must be purged before soft launch.
modes.humanGates: Decisions that always belong to a person
modes.supervisedNote: Raising a domain to supervised autonomy needs a second person and active spending caps.
modes.violationsFound: The current modes contradict the lifecycle: {items}.

modules.title: Modules
modules.lede: Which product modules are on in this hub, what each builds on, and how far the engine has built it.
modules.disableNote: Switching a module off hides it from participants; existing records stay and come back when it is switched on again.

legal.title: Legal and operator
legal.lede: The operator of the hub and the documents participants accept; a version becomes active only with counsel approval in every hub language.
legal.fakeScreening: fake adapter, not a real screening
legal.nothingToActivate: No version is approved by counsel and waiting for activation.
legal.templatesNote: A new version starts from the engine's templates; counsel reviews it before activation.

residency.title: Residency and sub-processors
residency.lede: Where personal data is stored and processed, and who processes it for the hub.
residency.contradiction: {services} run outside {country}, the residency country. Check whether personal data reaches them.
residency.privateOutside: A sub-processor outside the residency country receives private data; review the egress rules.
residency.subProcessorsNote: Generated from the hub's connections; every connection in this demo is a fake or manual adapter.
residency.newCountryHelp: Two-letter country code, for example US.

country.title: Country base
country.lede: The country facts the hub relies on: the bound country pack or the generic profile, and the hub's local additions.
country.generic: Generic profile: ISO data only; add identifiers, registers and other facts as local additions.
country.sourcesNote: Every fact in a pack cites its source and states how far it is verified.
country.label: Name
country.export: Export the additions as a country-pack change:
country.keyHelp: A stable key, for example US-CA:cslb.
country.candidateNote: A new addition stays a candidate until the compliance officer confirms it with a source.

taxonomy.title: Taxonomy and units
taxonomy.lede: Topics, categories, plan-step categories and units with their names in every hub language, released as versions.
taxonomy.empty: No taxonomy yet. Start with topics and plan-step categories; the engine's open plan-step taxonomy can be imported.
taxonomy.deprecateNote: Deprecating a term that is in use requires mapping it to another term first.
taxonomy.label: Name

launch.title: Launch checklist
launch.lede: What stands between the hub and soft launch or public. Every gate needs evidence; there is no waiver.
launch.noWaiver: No control waives a gate; an invalidated gate blocks like an open one until it is checked again.

gates.two_staff_with_second_factor: Two staff members with a second factor
gates.i18n_complete: Interface complete in every hub language

launch.evidenceHelp: The identifier of the stored evidence, for example ev-counsel-letter-2.
launch.publicBlocked: {count, plural, one {# gate still blocks going public.} other {# gates still block going public.}}

projects.title: Projects
projects.lede: Whether participants may publish projects and which fields a published project may show. Projects are private by default.
projects.publicFields: Fields a published project may show
projects.privateByDefault: Budgets, private files and contacts are never public, never in search and never sent to other hubs.
projects.disputesLink: Disputes are handled under a dispute grant in Support
projects.holdNote: A hold hides the public version under moderation; the owner is told why and may appeal.
projects.narrowerOnly: Only fields of the engine's public list can be allowed; the hub can narrow it, never widen it.

planner.title: Planner
planner.lede: Plan templates per country and project type. A participant's agent turns a template into a private plan; plan items become requests only after the owner confirms.
planner.blockedCycle: Template {template} cannot be published: item {item} depends on itself through a chain of steps.
planner.blockedMissing: Template {template} cannot be published: item {item} is missing.
planner.noTemplates: No templates yet. Hub experts draft them; a different person reviews and publishes.
planner.notLegalAdvice: Templates cite their regulatory references and are not legal advice.
planner.notByAuthor: A template is published by a reviewer who is not one of its authors.
planner.keyHelp: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, for example kitchen_remodel.
planner.settings: How far an agent may adapt a template
planner.ownerConfirms: Whatever the agent adapts, the plan is the owner's private project and the owner confirms it.

marketplace.title: Marketplace
marketplace.lede: Consultation and task categories: who may offer, how it is priced, what agents may do, and the commission as a versioned fee.
marketplace.windows: cancel within {hours} h, dispute within {days} d
marketplace.automation: Draft requests: {drafts}; accept within a mandate: {accepts}; {perWeek} requests a week
marketplace.noRules: No categories yet. Add a category before participants can request consultations or tasks.
marketplace.paused: Providers paused for an expired licence
marketplace.licensedNote: Licensed categories accept only verified providers; agents accept within a mandate only with verified counterparties.
marketplace.noFees: No commissions. Without a fee version nothing is charged.
marketplace.feesDisclosed: Every active fee is on the public price page; commissions never affect who is matched or in which order.

knowledgeSharing.title: Shared knowledge
knowledgeSharing.lede: Completed projects shared as diaries, templates, questions and lessons: published only with everyone's consent, after review, without private fields.
knowledgeSharing.privateExcluded: Budgets, prices and private files removed
knowledgeSharing.publishDisabled: Publishing is unavailable until every named party has consented.
knowledgeSharing.noShares: No shares are waiting. Owners propose them from their completed projects.
knowledgeSharing.guard: Withdrawing consent unpublishes the share and leaves a tombstone.

events.title: Events
events.lede: Who may host events, which events wait for review, and counts. Attendee lists and online links are never public.
events.payoutsLink: Payouts are released by a second person under Plans and payments
events.noReview: No events are waiting for review.
events.guard: Sponsors never affect listing position; there are no public event ratings.

policies.verified_and_editorial: Verified companies and the editorial team

learning.title: Learning
learning.lede: Course review, certificate counts and accreditations with their sources. Learning progress is private; there is no employer view.
learning.private: A certificate is never presented as a state licence.
learning.noAccreditations: No accreditation is recorded. None is shown without a source.
learning.noReview: No courses are waiting for review.
learning.certificateRefHelp: The reference printed on the certificate; the holder is told the reason category.
learning.sourceHelp: An https address where the accreditation can be checked.

matching.title: Matching
matching.lede: The needs board, introduction quotas and released method versions. Payment never changes who is matched or in which order.
matching.quotaShared: The quota is shared by a person and their agent.
matching.noMethods: No method version is released yet.
matching.noDraftMethod: No draft method version is waiting for release.
matching.samePlans: The quota is the same for every plan; it cannot be bought.

commerce.title: Commerce
commerce.lede: Category rules and the health of RFQs, quotes, agreements and orders, without budgets, floors or negotiations.
commerce.toFirstQuote: Median time to the first quote
commerce.toOrder: Median time from acceptance to order
commerce.evidenceHelp: The provider's reference that proves the outcome, for example a payment confirmation number.
commerce.noBlindRetry: An unknown outcome is reconciled with evidence, never retried blindly.
commerce.caseGrant: Help a party through a case grant in Support

modules.title: Agent modules
modules.lede: What every participant's agent can do in this hub: modules, capabilities per participant type and plan, defaults and maximums, jobs, model routes, limits and prices.
modules.noAgentList: This page configures the agent product for everyone. There is no list of anyone's agent here, and no way to open or change one participant's agent, mandates or settings.
modules.noModules: No agent modules are switched on in this hub yet.
modules.negativeMargin: The sale price is below the cost price: every unit is subsidised.
modules.commitmentBlocked: This module commits money: it can be active only for verified companies and with a second person.
modules.routesLink: Routes are set under Keys and models
modules.limitsValue: {runs} runs and {actions} actions a day, {concurrent} at once, {tokens} tokens a month
modules.noPrice: No price: the module is included in plans only.
modules.parity: A capability turned off disappears from the agent, the person's connected AI chat and the interface alike.
modules.tightenOnly: Participants may tighten any default in their own agent settings, never go above the hub maximum. A hub default never widens an existing mandate.
modules.jobsNote: A participant turns a job on only through a mandate proposal they confirm.
modules.toggleNote: Turning a capability off stops new runs and actions at the next authority check; runs already executing finish or go to reconciliation.
modules.capabilitySwitchProposed: A switch for a single capability is proposed and not built yet; until then, turn the capability off in a draft version.
modules.pricesLink: Prices per module, capability and model are set under Plans and payments

settings.approval_above_items: Ask the owner above this many items

jobTemplates.find_consultants_for_step: Find consultants for a plan step

policy.title: Agent policy
policy.lede: Hub-wide rules on top of modules: actions that are never pre-authorized, outreach, channels, disclosure in every hub language, plan-to-people limits and the settings of each jurisdiction.
policy.competition: Agents of competing sellers never exchange prices, and the platform never relays one seller's quote to another.
policy.draftRequests: Agents may draft consultation and task requests
policy.acceptWithinMandate: Agents may accept within a mandate (verified counterparties only)
policy.requestsPerWeek: Requests per week per participant's agent
policy.noDisclosure: No disclosure text yet; agents cannot send messages until it exists in every hub language.
policy.samePlans: Protection limits are the same for every plan and cannot be bought.

limits.envelopesPerCounterpartyPerDay: Agent messages per counterparty per day

policy.jurisdictionsLede: Disclosure, liability, consent, record-keeping and limits per jurisdiction, each beside the country pack's sourced default. When two jurisdictions apply, the more protective setting wins.
policy.noJurisdictions: No jurisdiction settings yet: the country pack's defaults apply.
policy.notLegalAdvice: The hub's counsel reviews the wording; a default is never legal advice.
policy.disclosureHelp: Shown on every message an agent prepares.
policy.jurisdictionHelp: A country or region code, for example US-CA.
policy.comparisonLabel: Compared with the country pack default
policy.neverWeaker: A hub may be stricter than a mandatory pack rule, never weaker; activation needs a second person and the disclosure in every hub language.

extensions.title: Extensions
extensions.lede: Functions, tools and integrations the hub adds to every participant's agent, each declared in full and activated only after a passing safety suite and a second person.
extensions.none: No extensions. Modules shipped with the engine still work.
extensions.oneAgent: An extension is one more ability of the participant's one agent, never a separate agent; participants configure it in their own agent settings.
extensions.safetyFailed: The safety suite failed on the fake adapter: activation is blocked until it passes.
extensions.withFake: with a fake for tests and dry runs:
extensions.guards: What an extension can never bypass
extensions.activationBlocked: Activation needs a passing safety suite on the fake adapter.
extensions.fakeOnly: The suite runs on the fake adapter only; it never calls the real endpoint.
extensions.suspendNote: Suspending is immediate and needs one person; activating again needs a second person.
extensions.keyHelp: Lower-case letters, digits and underscores, for example permit_lookup.
extensions.endpointHelp: Host name only, for example api.partner.example.
extensions.countryHelp: Two letters, for example US. Endpoints in restricted places are refused.
extensions.cannotBypass: An extension can add actions; it can never bypass mandates, budgets, approvals, kill switches, privacy rules, restricted places or the rule that untrusted text never issues commands.

external.title: External agents
external.lede: How participants' own agent software may connect through MCP and A2A: always as that person's agent, under their mandates, within these limits.
external.noList: Staff see counts only. There is no list of who connected which client; a support case with a case grant can inspect one registration when the participant asks for help.
external.representatives: Company representatives may use external clients
external.mandatesApply: Every state-changing call is checked against the person's current mandates exactly like their built-in agent.
external.adminSecondPerson: turning it on needs a second person
external.ratesValue: read {read}, draft {draft}, public {public}; {commits} commitments an hour
external.tightenOnly: Every value stays within engine bounds and can only be tightened here.

usage.title: Usage
usage.lede: Is the agent product useful, safe and affordable? Aggregates per module and cohort only: no person, no prompt, no output.
usage.noDrillDown: There is no drill-down to individuals and no per-company leaderboard.
usage.exportNote: The export holds the same aggregates as this page, with the same suppression.

abuse.title: Abuse
abuse.lede: Aggregate signals that open cases. Apart from rate throttling nothing is applied automatically; sanctions follow the moderation ladder with appeal rights.
abuse.noAutoSanctions: A signal never sanctions anyone by itself.
abuse.caseNote: The case goes to moderation with the aggregate signal, never with message content.
abuse.activate: Saved thresholds apply from the next evaluation.

responses.quota_reduction: Temporary quota reduction by the published rule
responses.security_event: Security event; repeated patterns open a case

offers.title: Offers and plans
offers.lede: Plan versions buy capacity for the payer's own work: modules, quotas, connections, trials. They never buy ranking, matching or reputation.
offers.noFreeMinimum: No free minimum is set; the engine's floor applies.
offers.freeStaysFree: Free minimum participation stays free in every plan.
offers.trialDays: {count, plural, =0 {No trial} one {# day} other {# days}}
offers.neutral: A plan has no field that could change ranking, matching, recommendations, reputation or verification; protective limits are the same for every plan.

prices.title: Prices
prices.lede: Prices per module, capability or model, with the cost price beside the sale price and the margin. A markup is computed once when drafted and stored as a fixed price.
prices.costChanged: A new cost record ({cost} from {date}) makes this margin {margin}. Nothing changed for participants; draft a new version if the price should follow:
prices.subject: Priced item
prices.none: No prices yet. Without an active price version nothing can be charged.
prices.readOnlyActive: A published version cannot be changed; create a new one. Versions never overlap and are never back-dated.
prices.saleHelp: For a flat price, in cents with up to six decimals, for example 12 or 0.3.
prices.percentHelp: For a markup: the sale price is computed now from the current cost and stored as a fixed number.
prices.noOverlap: Activation needs a second person; existing payers get advance notice of an increase.

invoices.title: Invoices
invoices.lede: Invoice runs, their states and totals by offer. Every line names its price version and meter.
invoices.noMoneyHeld: The platform never holds participants' money: charges, refunds and payouts run only through the hub's licensed payment provider. Demo: no money moves.
invoices.linesNameVersions: Commercial staff see invoice lines, never activity timelines.
invoices.retryNote: Issuance is idempotent: a retry never issues an invoice twice.

payouts.title: Payouts
payouts.lede: Payout batches to organizers, authors and experts, released by a second person and paid by the licensed provider.
payouts.provider: Payouts are paid by the hub's licensed payment provider; the platform and the operator never hold the money. Demo: no money moves.
payouts.evidenceHelp: The provider's reference for the payout.
payouts.noBlindRetry: An unknown outcome is reconciled with evidence, never retried blindly.

credits.title: Credits and refunds
credits.lede: Credits issued within role caps, credit packs whose validity is shown before purchase, and refund policy versions.
credits.roleCap: Cap per credit for your role
credits.neverSilent: Credits never expire silently: validity is shown before purchase and holders are reminded before any expiry.
credits.accountHelp: From the support case or invoice line; the credit appears on that account's next invoice.
credits.capHelp: Up to {cap} per credit for your role.
credits.expiresAfter: Expires after a number of days
credits.shownBeforePurchase: The validity and the refund policy are shown to the buyer before purchase.

tax.title: Tax
tax.lede: How the hub's own fees are taxed, with a source for each rule, and e-invoicing settings.
tax.advice: Decide tax treatment with tax advice; the console records it, it does not give advice.
tax.regionHelp: A country or region code, for example US-TX.
tax.sourceHelp: An https address of the rule or the advice it is based on.

senders.title: Senders
senders.lede: Sending domains and their DNS records, the reply-to address and the text message sender registration.
senders.none: No sending domain yet. Add one to send e-mail.
senders.domainHelp: The domain the hub sends from, for example mail.example.org.

templates.title: Templates
templates.lede: Message templates by category, with versions and languages. A template cannot be activated while a hub language is missing.
templates.synthetic: Previews use synthetic data only, never a participant's message.
templates.activateNote: Activation checks that every hub language exists.

deliverability.title: Deliverability
deliverability.lede: Delivery, bounce and complaint rates per template and channel. Never per person, and no open tracking.
deliverability.noTracking: There is no per-person open tracking.
deliverability.transactional: Transactional notices cannot be turned off by participants; pausing one stops it for everyone until it is fixed.

announcements.title: Announcements
announcements.lede: Announcements go only to people who opted in; legal notices go to everyone they concern. Each shows its lawful basis.
announcements.optedIn: No marketing without a recorded lawful basis.
announcements.basisShown: The lawful basis is checked before sending.

product.dateHelp: A date after today, as YYYY-MM-DD. Versions are never back-dated.
product.secondPersonAction: Another staff member approves it on the Approvals page as “{action}”.
product.pendingRequests: {count, plural, one {# request of this kind is waiting for a second person.} other {# requests of this kind are waiting for a second person.}}
product.wideScreen: More comfortable on a wide screen.

preview.title: Stored preview of the effect
preview.noticeDays: {days, plural, one {# day before it applies} other {# days before it applies}}
preview.privacy: Counts only: no participant is named, and any count below 10 is shown as “fewer than 10”. The second person approves exactly this preview.

guardRails.title: Guard rails no setting can switch off
guardRails.lede: These rules hold in every hub. No setting, price, plan, extension or kill switch here can weaken them.

items.mandates: Agents act only under the person's own structured mandates; chat text never authorizes
items.confirmations: The person confirms every commitment where the confirmation policy requires it
items.sanctions: Sanctions screening gates on money, commitments, counterparties and agents stay on
items.restrictedPlaces: Restricted places are refused for connections, model regions and extension endpoints
items.paymentNeutrality: No price, plan, credit or commission changes ranking, matching, recommendations or reputation
items.noImpersonation: Staff never act as a participant
items.noPerPersonAgents: Staff never read or change one participant's agent, mandates, settings, goals, jobs or connections
items.privateData: Private data stays private: egress is denied by default and staff see it only under a case grant

setup.title: Setup
setup.resume: Your answers are stored on the server, so you can stop and resume with the same link. In this demo nothing is stored.

check.title: Install check
check.purpose: The engine checks the address, database, object storage, worker, clock and secret store before anything else.

help.address: Set the public address to HTTPS (or localhost for a trial).
help.database: Run the migrations; the runtime role must not bypass row-level security.
help.object_storage: The bucket must allow write, read and delete, and must not be public.
help.worker: Start the background worker; no heartbeat was seen in the last minute.
help.clock: The server clock differs from your browser's by more than 30 seconds; signatures and schedules depend on it.
help.secret_store: Set a real key-encryption key; placeholders are refused.

check.blocking: A blocking check failed, so setup cannot continue.
check.cannotContinue: Setup cannot continue until every blocking check passes.

node.title: Node identity
node.purpose: The installation's name, domain and jurisdiction, and its signing key.
node.name: Node name
node.jurisdictionHelp: The country whose law the node operator follows. Restricted places are never offered.
node.key: A signing key is generated when you continue. Only its public key and fingerprint are ever shown; the private key never is.

hub.title: Hub identity
hub.purpose: Configure your country or city without code: starting point, territory, name in every language, languages, currency and time zone.
hub.exampleNote: Example values are synthetic; replace them with yours.
hub.startHelp: A country pack brings regions, identifier formats, currency and legal facts; the generic profile brings ISO data only.
hub.territoryHelp: A country, region or place code, for example US-CA:san-diego.
hub.name: Hub name
hub.nameHelp: Required in every hub language; you can add the other languages in the console.
hub.languagesHelp: Language tags, the default first, for example en, es.

operator.title: Operator
operator.purpose: The legal entity that operates the hub, its contacts, its ownership declaration and its sanctions screening.
operator.ownership: I declare the operator's ownership truthfully.
operator.screening: Screening runs on the engine's baseline list. With the fake adapter the result is labelled “fake: not a real screening”; a potential match opens a review that the operator cannot close.

admin.title: First administrator
admin.purpose: The first staff member, with a mandatory second factor and recovery codes shown once.
admin.name: Name
admin.passwordHelp: In this demo the name, e-mail and password never leave this page.
admin.secondFactorHelp: A second factor is mandatory; setup cannot finish without it.
admin.recoveryCodes: Ten single-use recovery codes appear here once, after the second factor is enrolled. In this demo none are generated.
admin.stored: I have stored the recovery codes.
admin.reducedSod: With one staff member the hub runs in reduced separation of duties; two-person actions wait until a second staff member joins.

residency.title: Storage and residency
residency.purpose: Where personal data is stored and processed, and which privacy regime the notices follow.
residency.countryHelp: Database, object storage and backups should be located there.
residency.egress: By default no non-public data leaves the residency country and nothing non-public goes to an external model provider until you allow it.

providers.title: Providers
providers.purpose: Every capability starts on its fake adapter, so the hub can be explored without accounts or costs.
providers.liveLater: Live connections are never made here: they need a passing synthetic test, an egress decision and a second person.
providers.models: For language models you can later connect a provider directly or through OpenRouter, an optional router.
providers.invite: To invite the second staff member before e-mail is live, the console shows a one-time invitation link that expires in 72 hours.

modes.title: Modes
modes.purpose: How the hub starts: data mode, registration, modules, moderation and automation.
modes.defaults: Registration starts closed, every automation domain manual, indexing off; publications, magazine, events, search and communications are on. Change them later in the console.

review.title: Review
review.purpose: A summary of every step before you finish. Finishing records the configuration, creates the launch gates and invalidates the setup token.
review.afterFinish: After finishing, the hub is a draft: registration closed, every provider fake, indexing off.
